summary: Wired the ground-truth oracle. The magnetar clone holds real (LFS-fetched) binaries: Revit_IFC5_Einhoven.rvt (Revit 2023, no IFC shipped -> oracle = FME/StrangeMatter CSVs carrying Revit UniqueIds) and 2024_Core_Interior.rvt (Revit 2024, oracle = IFC Exports/2024_Core_Interior_slim.ifc, whose VersionGUID equals the rvt's Unique Document GUID; plus a 2-element mini export). Built tests/oracle/{rvt_release,oracle_extract,oracle_ifc,compare_oracle,schema_drift}.py + README + pytest gate, all cached (cold run ~2.5 s). Confirmed the wave-1 grammar is release-independent (4,140/4,195/4,386 classes for 2023/2024/2026, same single desync at VarExpr.m_refCt at ~95%), and — the key structural result — our schema type ids ARE the on-disk class words in every release: all Partitions framing tags resolve BY CLASS NAME (SegmentMarker/SegmentCheckback/SignatureMarker/ContentMarker/ContentKey), so a name-parametric walker reads 2023/2024/2026 partitions with 100% CRC and 100% record-walk coverage. Discovered ElementId is 32-bit pre-2024 (record + ElemTable layouts) and that vendor/rvt-rs's 11-release drift CSV equals our id +1 in all 219 comparable cells. First agreement report: 1,055/1,055 (100%) IFC elements found in the .rvt by ElementId (Tag), yielding CONFIRMED per-element correspondences (IfcWall<->SWall, IfcDoor/Window/Column<->FamilyInstance, IfcSlab/ShadingDevice<->Floor, IfcOpeningElement<->FamilyInstance|CurveElem, IfcBuildingStorey<->Level, IfcSpace<->RoomElem, IfcSite<->SiteSurface, IfcWallType<->BasicWallType, IfcSlabType<->FloorAttributes, family types<->FamilySymbol/Family/FamilySurrogate, materials<->MaterialElem) and 100% name agreement (15/15 storeys, 4/4 wall types, 12/12 family types, 116/116 spaces, 9/9 materials); Einhoven: 26/26 FME ElementIds resolve into ElemTable and partition records (hok.wall->SWall, curtain panels/window->FamilyInstance) with all 3 episode GUIDs in Global/History.
key_findings: Corpus reality: Einhoven .rvt is Revit 2023 (build 20230828_1515, 7 partitions) and 2024_Core_Interior .rvt is Revit 2024 (8 partitions); both are real CFB binaries (LFS objects present, no git lfs pull needed) and de-page with the 2026 stride (64896+353) with 100% gzip CRC. There is NO IFC for Einhoven in the dataset; its oracle is the FME Demos CSVs (SourceDataItemId = Revit UniqueId = episode GUID + hex ElementId, all 3 episode GUIDs are entries in the rvt's Global/History). Pair A identity is proven: 2024_Core_Interior_slim.ifc VersionGUID 2a619b2e-a277-4154-90ff-ca7b37baec5b == the rvt's Unique Document GUID (IFC NumberOfSaves 65 vs rvt central version 66).

Wave-1 schema grammar (src/rvt/schema_a) is release-independent: parses 4,140 (2023) / 4,195 (2024) / 4,386 (2026) classes, 11.2-11.8k fields, ~94.7% of each stream, and desyncs at the SAME class in every release (VarExpr.m_refCt, descriptor 04 00 04 00 = one missing grammar rule for a non-zero pad word), so the last ~5% is a single grammar gap, not per-release corruption. 99% of class names are shared between releases; only 2-5% keep the same id (median drift +41 for 2023->2024, +95 for 2024->2026) -> decode by class NAME, never numeric id.

Our type-id numbering (definition order + 0x0c) is externally proven to be the on-disk class word: in 2023/2024/2026 the Partitions header class = ContentMarker (0x365/0x37b/0x3a3), separator inner = ContentKey, block header/terminator = SegmentMarker (0xe4e/0xe7c/0xf28), block trailer = SegmentCheckback (0xe47/0xe75/0xf21), unit footer = SignatureMarker (0xe61/0xe8f/0xf3f), seq101 record class = ElementHeader (0x576/0x59f/0x5e5), seq103 = SerializedDummy/GElement; ADocument=0x1c in all. Hence a walker keyed by class name (tests/oracle/rvt_release.py) reads any release: 100% blocks CRC-valid and 100% record-walk on all three files.

vendor/rvt-rs's tag-drift-2016-2026.csv found and validated: all 219 comparable cells (122 classes x 2023/2024/2026) equal our id + 1 exactly (they read the 0x8000-flagged u16 after the class name; the byte-level evidence -- framing tags and record class words -- matches OUR value), and their 64 KiB scan cap yields only 122 classes vs our 4,100+; use their CSV with a -1 correction.

Release-dependent layouts discovered: ElementId is 32-bit in Revit <=2023 and 64-bit >=2024 (matches the public 2024 API ElementId(long) change) -> seq101 header 12 B / seq102-103 header 16 B pre-2024 (16/20 B after); Global/ElemTable records are 28 B pre-2024 {u32 orig, u32 id, u32 create_ep, u32 mod_ep, u32 user_ep, u32 part, i32 owner} vs 40 B >=2024; oracle_extract auto-detects both. Also the Partitions header's last u32 is that partition's OWN element count, not the Global/ElemTable count (they coincided in the 2026 samples only because each had one partition).

Agreement report pair A (1,055 IFC elements with Revit ElementId tags): 1,055/1,055 (100%) found as seq102 object records AND in Global/ElemTable; CONFIRMED IfcWall<->SWall (360/360), IfcColumn<->FamilyInstance (256/256), IfcDoor<->FamilyInstance (132/132), IfcWindow<->FamilyInstance (6/6), IfcSlab<->Floor (79/80, +1 BuildingPad = 'Pad:Site Pad'), IfcShadingDevice<->Floor (20/20, canopies exported via slab-as-shading mapping), IfcOpeningElement MIXED 138 FamilyInstance (door/window inserts) / 63 CurveElem (sketched openings) -- a genuine two-source entity.

Name agreement pair A is total: 15/15 storey names live inside Level records (Basement 2 -> Level 16235 ... Level 13 -> 87622), 4/4 wall type names inside BasicWallType records, 12/12 family/type names (Column_Sqaure, I_Single-Flush, M_Single-Flush, Single Window / their types) inside FamilySymbol + Family + FamilySurrogate records, slab/pad types inside FloorAttributes/BuildingPadType, 116/116 IfcSpace names inside RoomElem records, 9/9 materials inside MaterialElem records, and the IfcSite name 'Surface:21971' ends in ElementId 21971 = a SiteSurface record. So system-family types serialize as *Attributes/*Type classes and loadable-family types as FamilySymbol.

Pair B (Einhoven 2023, FME oracle): 26 distinct ElementIds -> 26/26 in the 28-byte ElemTable and 26/26 as seq102 records; hok.wall.Properties (wall 2808=0xaf8) -> SWall, 24 hok.wall.curtainpanle -> FamilyInstance, ifc.window.casement (5317) -> FamilyInstance -- curtain panels are FamilyInstance and grid lines CurtainGridLine in 2023 too, and the 32-bit id / 28-byte ElemRec / 12+16-byte record layouts are confirmed by an external oracle.

Count matching alone does NOT identify classes for a real project (SWall live=1,209 vs 360 exported walls; FamilyInstance live=12,221 spans columns+doors+windows+panels+tags; distinct seq102 ids 49,173 vs 26,425 live ElemTable ids because 47 save units retain superseded versions) -- the element-id join is the confirming evidence; a live census (ElemTable ids, last record per id) is the correct model census and 'last record wins' is now measurable.

The harness is a cheap regression loop: JSON summaries cached by file mtime under tests/oracle/cache/ (3.5 MB), cold end-to-end ~2.5 s, warm 0.2 s; `pytest tests/oracle -q` = 10 assertions pinning identity match, 100% join coverage, five class correspondences at >=95% purity, 100% name agreement, 26/26 Einhoven resolution, and the release-independent walker (schema-sourced tags, all blocks CRC-ok, no errors) on both old releases.

confidence: High for everything reported. The element-id join is per-element ground truth (Revit's own exporter stamps IfcElement.Tag with the ElementId and the file with the document episode GUID) and it resolves 1,055/1,055 on the 2024 pair and 26/26 on the Einhoven FME pair, so the CONFIRMED class correspondences and the 32-vs-64-bit id / 28-vs-40-byte ElemRec / 12+16-byte pre-2024 record-header layouts are not hypotheses. The 'our type id == on-disk class word (rvt-rs is +1)' claim is proven by three independent releases where semantically-named framing classes (SegmentMarker, SignatureMarker, ContentMarker, ElementHeader) land exactly on the bytes that play those roles, and by 100% CRC / 100% record-walk under the name-resolved tags. Grammar release-independence is high confidence (same desync class in all releases at ~95%). Medium confidence / labelled MIXED: IfcOpeningElement's two-way split (real but only one model), IfcShadingDevice<->Floor (an export-mapping artefact of this model), and IfcSpace<->RoomElem which is a by-name (not by-id) confirmation because IfcSpace carries no Tag.
open_questions: The Partitions stream-header u32 is the partition's own element count; the meaning of the multiple Partitions/N in non-workshared 2023/2024 files (Einhoven 0-6, Core Interior 46-65) and how elements distribute across them (worksets vs. document increments vs. links) is not resolved by the oracle.

IfcSpace<->RoomElem is confirmed by name only (IfcSpace has no Tag/ElementId in Revit's export); confirming by id needs the RoomElem body decoded (room number/name fields) or the space's IfcRelSpaceBoundary walls.

Curtain-wall decomposition is unverified: the Einhoven host wall 2808 is an SWall with 24 FamilyInstance panels and Core Interior has 5,112 CurtainGridLine records, but no IfcCurtainWall exists in either export, so panel/grid/mullion structure has no IFC-side ground truth here.

The schema grammar gap at VarExpr.m_refCt (descriptor 04 00 04 00) hides the final ~5% of the class map in every release; a few electrical/MEP classes may live there (Wall, PanelBoard, TopographySurface, MEPCurve are not serialized class names -- SWall, SiteSurface, FamilyInstance are).

Whether 'the last-written seq102 record per ElementId is the live version' holds universally (the join assumed it and passed 1,055/1,055, but Partitions/46 keeps ~2x superseded versions across 47 save units) needs the object decoder plus save-unit ordering to nail down.

The 20 KB Revit/2024_Core_Interior.ifc has a VersionGUID (dbf4e41a...) not present in the rvt's History yet its 2 elements resolve into the rvt -- what Revit stamps as VersionGUID for a filtered/by-element export is unclear.
